ActionIntent.title: action-intent
ActionIntent.description: NexLoop target contract; server-derived identity required. This is not an existing upstream EIOS/Pi API.

CandidateDefinition.title: candidate-definition
CandidateDefinition.description: ADR-019. A proposed new ontology definition or instance that did not match the recalled schema/instances. Staged for merge or human review; never applied directly. Server-derived identity required. Not an existing upstream API.

Claim.title: claim
Claim.description: NX-019. One evidence-bound Claim extracted from persisted conversation Messages: candidate knowledge, never a formal business object. Identity, tenant, world, consumer and evidence are server-derived; extractors never produce verified_fact. Not an existing upstream API.

mode.description: Derived from world_id by the server, never supplied by a caller: world real -> real; worlds simulation and shadow -> simulation; any other world -> test. The enum matches the other contracts; shadow is excluded below.

ref.description: consumer: server-derived consumer object id; otherwise empty

text.description: referent words present in the topic window, or empty

condition.description: verbatim condition clause; required when modality=conditional

anchor.description: server acceptance time of the cited Message

normalization.description: Owner 2026-10-17: how the time was read. Present when the extraction model proposed an absolute reading: source (rule: the proposal was refused or not used; llm: the rules could not read it and the checked proposal stands; llm+rule: both agree; conflict: both read it differently, neither chosen), verdict (accepted, agreed, conflict, or the refusal code), both readings and the model's stated assumptions. Absent on Claims extracted before it.

span_start.description: Unicode code point offset into the Message body

content_hash.description: sha256 of the full Message body (UTF-8)

correlation_key.description: same consumer+kind+predicate+normalized value+polarity; links repeats, never deduplicates

allOf.description: extractors never produce verified_fact; only verification channels may, outside this contract
claims are derived per world and never carry shadow mode (shadow worlds project as simulation)

CommitmentView.title: commitment-view
CommitmentView.description: NX-028 (D8). The owner workbench's read projection of one Commitment (NX-026 runtime.nexloop_commitment_view). `status` lives only in `properties.status`; the interface never infers it. The four evidence columns are separate: a delivered message proves delivery only, never fulfilment (AT-040); `problem_resolved` is unavailable in v0.1 (NX-026 D5). `quote` is the promised words, shown only while the source Message exists AND the reader holds that Message's READ (`quote_status`: ok, restricted = withheld for lack of READ, unavailable = source deleted, none = no source message). Server-derived; grants nothing. Optional `consumer_display` (walkthrough 2026-10-18 F03/F04, D3): the customer's name state as the workbench decides it for every page (ok with the name read through the per-property READ; restricted with reason forbidden or withheld, never saying whether a name exists; missing; failed). It grants nothing and is absent from older servers.

ContactRestrictionView.title: contact-restriction-view
ContactRestrictionView.description: NX-028 (D8). The owner workbench's read projection of contact restrictions and reply escalations (ADR-023, 0109). A refusal hit's `matched_text` is the customer's own words: it is present only when the reader also holds that Message's READ (`matched_text_status` ok), otherwise null with status restricted (shown as "rule <rule_id> matched; text needs authorization"). Only the owner can release a restriction (ADR-023 §2.4); a release never replays refused intents. Server-derived; grants nothing.

ContextManifest.title: context-manifest
ContextManifest.description: NexLoop target contract; server-derived identity required. This is not an existing upstream EIOS/Pi API.

ContextPackV6.title: context-pack-v6
ContextPackV6.description: NX-023 Context pack v6. Message Runs: the frozen v2 core (bindings, user_statement, formal_facts, current_constraints, supply), or the v4 core when the optional relationship_context section is present (current statements are resolved user statements only; hypotheses are evidence only), re-derived by SQL at bind; Role Runs: the frozen v3/v5 core under role and a service-trigger current_event, plus strategy, goal/control snapshot, labelled item sections, budget report and explicit insufficiency. Every item cites its source revision, canonical content hash and the current READ decision it was read under; SQL re-verifies each against the source row. Formal sections carry only governed objects/policy/ledger state; Claims under review appear only as source text; hypotheses never enter a real-world Context. No floating-point numbers. Server-assembled; grants nothing. v2-v5 stay frozen and old Runs keep using them.

operator_persona.description: 0227 operator persona slice 1 (docs/design/operator-persona-design.md): how the operator speaks to this Consumer, persona@version, re-derived and checked by SQL at bind; absent when the tenant has no usable persona.

preferences.description: 0228: the consumer's own communication preferences (from their Claims, not dismissed by the owner); data for the model; quiet hours, frequency, channel and topic are also enforced at dispatch.

outreach.description: Outreach slice 5 (docs/design/proactive-outreach.md §3.3): only in a plan reevaluation Run whose Role execution ceiling holds nexloop.outreach.send:1; the purposes this tenant has enabled in the current purpose list and the tenant's marketing state, re-derived and checked by SQL at bind. Whether to contact the customer at all is the Run's judgement (no_action is normal); every gate is rechecked at dispatch.

ConversationMessage.title: conversation-message
ConversationMessage.description: NX-051 (AT-014). The read projection of one conversation Message, as the conversation read API returns it. `sequence` and `accepted_at` are this system's receipt order and time (assigned at commit, never rewritten). `provider` is the channel's own order, time and reference as evidence (trust: server = produced here, signed = a verified signed channel, client = what the browser client stated; client values never order anything and are never a time anchor). `reply_to_message_id` is the resolved reply target in the same conversation: for an Agent reply it mirrors the server-derived trigger_message_id; for an inbound message it is the reference the channel carried, once resolved (null while pending, for another conversation, or none). Server-derived; grants nothing. NX-028 (ruling B, approved contract change): an outbound message is an Agent reply (sender_kind=agent, with its governed intent_id) or a staff reply written during the author's own takeover of a native WebChat conversation (sender_kind=human_takeover, no intent: it does not go through the effect ledger); both carry the server-checked trigger_message_id.

accepted_at.description: This system's acceptance time as stored with the Message (PostgreSQL timestamptz text).

EventEnvelope.title: event-envelope
EventEnvelope.description: NexLoop target contract; server-derived identity required. This is not an existing upstream EIOS/Pi API.

EvolutionCandidate.title: evolution-candidate
EvolutionCandidate.description: NexLoop target contract; server-derived identity required. This is not an existing upstream EIOS/Pi API.

EvolutionEvaluationBundle.title: evolution-evaluation-bundle
EvolutionEvaluationBundle.description: NX-038 E5 (design §12.4, §7; D7, D18, D19): the frozen evaluation bundle NX-038 hands to NX-039 with a proposed evolution candidate. Built in SQL from the stored candidate (authz.nexloop_evo_bundle_freeze); ids, digests, versions and numbers only, never a message body, Claim value, prompt or patch text. NX-039 may not change any condition in it; a changed condition is a new candidate. `case_groups` maps every case to its Consumer or session cluster so NX-039 can re-check that no cluster is on both sides (AT-048). The bundle_digest is the sha256 the database computes over the stored value. NexLoop target contract; server-derived identity required. This is not an existing upstream EIOS/Pi API.

EvolutionEvaluationReport.title: evolution-evaluation-report
EvolutionEvaluationReport.description: NX-038 E5 (design §12.4, §7; D7): the evaluation report of one frozen evolution-evaluation-bundle at one level (L0 deterministic replay in NX-038; L1 belongs to NX-039). Every frozen hard gate is answered pass or fail with evidence ids, separately from the scores; `accept` requires every gate passed, and an equal score is never an acceptance (D7). Missing inputs end `incomplete`, never a pass. Ids, codes, scores and numbers only; never a message body, Claim value, prompt or patch text. The report digest goes to the candidate event log and review links (D4). A report changes no candidate status. NexLoop target contract; server-derived identity required. This is not an existing upstream EIOS/Pi API.

hard_gates_version.description: NX-039 V2: the frozen gate version the report answers (optional, additive).

failed_gates.description: NX-039 V2: the failed gates in registry order; each gate id is its own rejection code (optional, additive).

change_class.description: NX-039 V2 (D39-7): decided by classify_change, never set by a person or an Agent; major and refused are always rejected (optional, additive).

reproduced.description: NX-039 V2 (D39-2): the second L0 pass gave the same report (optional, additive).

OntologyMutation.title: ontology-mutation
OntologyMutation.description: NexLoop target contract; server-derived identity required. This is not an existing upstream EIOS/Pi API.

OutreachPurposes.title: outreach-purposes
OutreachPurposes.description: Proactive outreach purpose list (docs/design/proactive-outreach.md §2, owner decisions P2/P5/P8; outreach slice 3): trusted, versioned configuration. A purpose not in the current list cannot be used; plan-defined purposes must be registered here first. The owner enables or disables a listed purpose per tenant; nobody adds one at run time.

requires_consent.description: Marketing only: true makes this purpose opt-in even when the tenant is opt-out.

requires_approval.description: Owner approval before dispatch (outreach slice 6); default false (P5).

default_enabled.description: Enabled for a tenant until the owner changes it.

OutreachSend.title: outreach-send
OutreachSend.description: Proactive outreach send request (docs/design/proactive-outreach.md §3.1, owner decision P1; outreach slice 4): the parameters of the governed Action nexloop.outreach.send:1 and the request the server freezes from them. The caller never chooses the topic, the purpose version, the origin kind or the business intent id: the server derives them (topic and version from the current purpose list; intent id = sha256 of tenant, consumer, purpose, origin_ref and the day in the tenant time zone). Every dispatch gate is rechecked at dispatch; the Action is external and its real dispatch switch is closed by default.

purpose.description: A purpose of the current outreach purpose list, enabled for the tenant.

origin_ref.description: What the send follows from: a commitment, a receipt intent, a plan or the owner's own request.

body.description: The message text; the purpose's content_rules.max_chars also applies.

channel.description: v1: the native WebChat channel only.

conversation_id.description: Optional (P4): continue this conversation of the consumer; otherwise the server chooses.

frozen.description: Server-derived, never accepted from the caller.

ReviewDecision.title: review-decision
ReviewDecision.description: ADR-019. A human reviewer's decision on a candidate-definition. Reviewer identity is server-derived from an authenticated human session; the decision itself is a governed human Action and is audited. Not an existing upstream API.

RunCommand.title: run-command
RunCommand.description: NexLoop target contract; server-derived identity required. This is not an existing upstream EIOS/Pi API.

RunOutcome.title: run-outcome
RunOutcome.description: NX-024. The result a plan reevaluation Run records through its Host for the current plan version. no_action, needs_information, waiting_external and escalate are normal results, not failures; plan_update supersedes the plan with new steps; action_intent names an intent this very Run submitted. Identity (tenant, world, Run, plan) is derived by the server from the Run's live activation; this body carries none. Grants nothing.

SchemaProposal.title: schema-proposal
SchemaProposal.description: NX-040 F2 (docs/implementation/NX-040-design.md §3, §9; D21-D27, owner 2026-10-20): the frozen content of one Schema proposal, the input of the EIOS Schema review. Built from one ontology_schema evolution candidate; it changes no Schema, publishes nothing and grants nothing. Frozen at creation: a changed change is a new proposal. Ids, digests, codes and counts only; the structured change itself is held by the server and named here by its digest. Evaluation state lives on the candidate; the proposal records only frozen, published or withdrawn.

candidate_id.description: The ontology_schema evolution candidate this proposal was frozen from.

operation.description: §4.1 whitelist; anything else is refused (add_relation_type is out of scope, D24).

parent_schema_version.description: The Object Type version the change applies to, fixed at freeze; 0 for a new Object Type.

parent_schema_digest.description: Digest of the parent definition, computed by the server at freeze.

input_snapshot_digest.description: The NX-038 diagnosis snapshot of the candidate.

permit_ref.description: The NX-039 release permit used when published; null until then.

TrajectorySample.title: trajectory-sample
TrajectorySample.description: NX-038 E2 (design §11.2, D10/D11): one trajectory sample a diagnosis reads, from either route with one shape: the database route (authz.nexloop_evo_trace_runs as nexloop_evo_reader; one issued Run) or the evidence-pack route (one NX-037 interaction record). Identifiers, codes, counts and times only: never a message body, Claim value, prompt, quote or credential. `persona` is the served Consumer's ADR-034 persona (D12, always labelled; null when the Run serves no Consumer or the record carries none); test-stack records never reach a formal diagnosis (§11.3). A sample is input to diagnosis, never a business fact. NexLoop target contract; server-derived identity required. This is not an existing upstream EIOS/Pi API.

WorkbenchArtifacts.title: workbench-artifacts
WorkbenchArtifacts.description: Enterprise world model W4 (data assets): one page of a tenant's stored local Artifacts for the owner workbench, GET /api/v1/workbench/artifacts (workbench read verb `artifacts`; owners and operators, ADR-025 / ADR-035). Metadata only: id, purpose (from the binding that holds it), media type, size, the first 12 hex digits of its sha256, created and retention times, the source Run and the owning Consumer id; never content, storage keys or upload details. Newest first; `next_before` is the cursor '<created_at>|<artifact_id>' of the page's last item. An Artifact of a Consumer being erased, or one an erasure is deleting, is not listed and is counted in `hidden`. Each listed Artifact is audited. NexLoop target contract; server-derived identity required. This is not an existing upstream EIOS/Pi API.

WorkbenchCapabilities.title: workbench-capabilities
WorkbenchCapabilities.description: Enterprise world model W3 (owner 2026-10-19): the owner workbench's read-only capability catalog of one tenant, GET /api/v1/workbench/capabilities (workbench read verb `capabilities`). Metadata only: the governed capability registry, the tenant's business Action definitions with their effect categories (undeclared means closed, customer contact by default), inbound channel namespaces, the effect Actions active catalog offerings deliver through (counts), and the real dispatch switches from the same SQL source as the metrics read. No consumer, message, intent or credential data. NexLoop target contract; server-derived identity required. This is not an existing upstream EIOS/Pi API.

WorkbenchObjectNeighbors.title: workbench-object-neighbors
WorkbenchObjectNeighbors.description: Enterprise world model W2 (owner 2026-10-19, D3): the depth-1 neighbourhood of one object, GET /api/v1/workbench/objects/{type}/{id}/neighbors (workbench read verb `object_neighbors`). Groups by direction, edge (a governed relation name, or `property:<name>` for a reference property) and neighbour type. At most 25 candidates a group are checked: a neighbour is listed only when its ADR-025 READ holds and, for a property edge, the READ of the referencing property; the other checked candidates are `invisible`, those beyond 25 are `collapsed` (not checked, not shown). Identifiers only. NexLoop target contract; server-derived identity required. This is not an existing upstream EIOS/Pi API.

WorkbenchObjectPage.title: workbench-object-page
WorkbenchObjectPage.description: Enterprise world model W2 (owner 2026-10-19): one page of a type's instances for the owner workbench, GET /api/v1/workbench/objects/{type} (workbench read verb `objects`). Identifiers, schema versions, revisions and update times; since D-G1 (owner 2026-10-20) each listed object also carries `properties`: per schema property its value when the member's per-property READ holds (read through the same audited object read), or its name only (withheld: an owner-restricted group, or a property the member's role does not derive), or missing. Each object is listed only when the member's ADR-025 READ derivation holds (an audited read); the others on the page are counted in `invisible`. `total` is the type's instance count in the tenant (metadata). NexLoop target contract; server-derived identity required. This is not an existing upstream EIOS/Pi API.

WorkbenchObjectValues.title: workbench-object-values
WorkbenchObjectValues.description: Workbench Object property values (L4 capability gap D-G1, owner 2026-10-20; ADR-025, ADR-035): GET /api/v1/workbench/objects/{type}/{id} (workbench verbs `object_fields` and the audited object read). Per schema property: its value (text, or canonical JSON text, at most 2000 characters, `truncated` when cut) when the member's per-property READ holds; withheld with its name only when the owner restricted its group (`restricted`) or the member's role does not derive it (`not_permitted`), or its value names a Consumer being erased (`erasing`); or missing. An object the member may not read, including one whose Consumer is being erased, is 403; every read is audited. NexLoop target contract; server-derived identity required. This is not an existing upstream EIOS/Pi API.

WorkbenchWorldModel.title: workbench-world-model
WorkbenchWorldModel.description: Enterprise world model W1 (docs/design/workbench-world-model-design.md; owner 2026-10-19 D1-D7). GET /api/v1/workbench/world-model: a read-only snapshot of the tenant's published model metadata for a workbench member holding nexloop.workbench.read (SQL authz.nexloop_workbench_read verb world_model). The current version of each object type (with its properties), relation type and event type; the active Actions and Functions of the read world; instance counts per type. Metadata only: no instance content. A property in an owner-restricted group is listed by name with withheld=true and nothing else (AT-003). Server-derived from the authenticated session; grants nothing; there is no write counterpart (schema changes stay candidate review and trusted configuration).
